message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for Atlantic Avenue.

I will bid $241 to win the auction. This gives me the only yellow property and leaves enough cash for a three-house New York. I will drop out if p2 raises further.

Bidding $241 leaves $697 cash, which clears the $650 target. Winning Atlantic makes me the veto player for the yellow group, preventing p2 from completing a monopoly with p4.

p2 has $1256 cash and is already bidding $240. They may raise further.

The real danger is p1 with three houses on New York Avenue. That yields $600 in rent. I must weigh that threat against the yellow monopoly risk.

I am still several spaces away from the orange properties. I will stay in the auction until the cash target is reached, then drop out.

p2 already holds Marvin Gardens, so Atlantic is worth full value to them. The list price is $260, making the current $240 bid below market. I will bid $241 to keep pressure and force them toward a higher overpay.

Bleeding p2 by forcing an overpay is ineffective with $1256 cash. The real value is the veto power. I can trade Atlantic later for Park Place.

Mortgaging Mediterranean and Electric yields an extra $105 cushion. Boardwalk mortgage adds another $200. I can survive one New York Avenue hit without selling anything. A $300 bid would leave only $38 cash after rent. I will not raise to the list price of $260 because p2 will match it.

I will not reveal my cash cap in the public message. I am also weighing whether p2's $240 bid is already too high, since they would pay $20 above list for two of three yellows and face roughly $150 in house costs to complete the set.

p4 has $513 and two of three greens. They previously dropped at $140 to block a cheap yellow set. If p2 wins, they still need p4's Ventnor to complete the monopoly. p4 could trade with p2 for Atlantic instead. I would hold only one of three yellows. That makes the auction more complex than a simple veto.

Winning the auction would create a 1-1-1 yellow split. Neither p2 nor p4 could complete the set alone, so they would both need to trade with me or with each other.
